Rashi on Pesachim 61a:10:1.hebrew: סורסי - ארמי, חכמי האומות קורין לו לינג"א שוריי"א (שפה סורית):
Rashi on Pesachim 61a:10:1.english: Sursi - Aramaic. The sages of the nations call it linga surya (the Syriac language).

Rashi on Pesachim 61a:10:2.hebrew: כוס - שחוט, למימרא דבשעת שחיטה צריך להתכוין למנויו:
Rashi on Pesachim 61a:10:2.english: Kos - Slaughter, meaning to say that at the time of slaughter one must have intention for its registrants.

Rashi on Pesachim 61a:11:1.hebrew: לפי אכלו - הראוי לאכול, פרט לחולה ולזקן ולערל, ואפילו הן מנויין:
Rashi on Pesachim 61a:11:1.english: According to his eating - [One] who is fit to eat, excluding a sick person, an elderly person, and an uncircumcised person, even if they are registered [for it].

Rashi on Pesachim 61a:1:1.hebrew: וישנו לאחר מיתה - מת, בנו מביא קרבן אביו, ואם שחטו שלא לשמו, לא עלה לשם חובה, ואחריות הקרבן מוטל על נכסי המת, וצריך להביא אחר. וישנו בקרבן צבור כקרבן יחיד:
Rashi on Pesachim 61a:1:1.english: And it applies after death - [If the owner] died, his son brings his father's offering, and if [one] slaughtered it not for its own sake, it does not count toward the obligation, and responsibility for the offering rests upon the deceased's estate, and [the son] must bring another. And it applies to a communal offering just as to an individual offering.

Rashi on Pesachim 61a:1:2.hebrew: אבל בשינוי בעלים - מחשב בדבר אחר הוא, ואינו בארבע עבודות. בשאר זבחים דלאו פסח, דלאו עיקרן לאכילה אתי אלא לכפרה, לא שייך שינוי בעלים אלא בזריקה, שאין לו בקרבן אלא כפרתו, וכפרה ליתא אלא בזריקה. וכי מרבינן שאר עבודות לפוסלה בשינוי בעלים בפ"ק דזבחים, לא מרבינן אלא שוחט להתכפר אחר בזריקת דמו, או מוליך או מקבל לזרוק לשם אחר, או זרק ממנו לשם אחר. אבל שוחט לשם אחר — שתהא השחיטה לבדה לשם אחרים, אבל בשעת שחיטה אין דעתו על הזריקה אלא לבעליו — כשר. והכי אמרי' התם: אמר רב אשי ק"ו: ומה אם במקום שאמר "הריני שוחט לשם פלוני" דכשר, שחטו לזרוק לשם פלוני פסול, מקום שאם אמר כו'. ש"מ מיהא דאין מחשבת שינוי בעלים בשאר עבודות, אא"כ מחשבין באחת מהן על מנת לזרוק. אבל בשינוי קודש, שחט שלא לשמו פסול, דכתיב: "זבח שלמים" — זביחה לשם שלמים; וכן בחטאת: "ושחט אותה לחטאת"; וכן פסח: "זבח פסח הוא". ומיהו ודאי פסח שעיקרו לבעליו ליאכל בא, שחטו שלא לשם בעליו להאכילו למנויין אחרים — פסול, כדקתני מתני': "שחטו שלא למנויו פסול". וע"כ בחישב על השחיטה לחודא קאמר, לא על מנת לזרוק, מדאיפלגו בה אמוראי בגמרא: "שחטו למולין על מנת שיתכפרו בו ערלים", מכלל ד"שחטו לערלים" דמתניתין במחשב על השחיטה קאמר, ו"שלא למנויו" דומיא ד"לערלים", דהא גבי הדדי קתני להו:
Rashi on Pesachim 61a:1:2.english: However, regarding a change of owners - [The priest] is thinking about another matter [i.e., not the offering itself], and it does not [apply] in [all] four services. With other sacrifices that are not the Pesach [offering] — whose primary purpose is not for eating, but rather for atonement — a change of owners is only relevant in the throwing [of the blood], for [the owner] has nothing in the sacrifice except his atonement, and atonement is only through the throwing [of the blood]. And when we include the other services to disqualify it through a change of owners in the first chapter of Zevachim, we only include one who slaughters [with the intention] that another [person] gain atonement through the throwing of its blood, or one who conveys or receives [the blood] in order to throw [it] for the sake of another, or one who threw [the blood] from it for the sake of another. However, one who slaughters for the sake of another — [intending] that the slaughtering alone be for the sake of others, while at the time of slaughtering his intention for the throwing [of the blood] is only for its [true] owners — [the offering] is valid. And thus we say there: Rav Ashi said an a fortiori [inference]: If in a case where he said, "Behold, I am slaughtering for the sake of so-and-so," where it is valid, [yet] if he slaughtered it in order to throw [its blood] for the sake of so-and-so it is invalid, then in a case where if he said, etc. We learn from this, at any rate, that there is no [disqualifying] intention of a change of owners in the other services unless one has [that] intention during one of them with the purpose of throwing [the blood for another]. However, regarding a change of sanctity, if he slaughtered [it] not for its own sake, it is invalid, as it is written: "a sacrifice of peace-offerings" — [meaning] the slaughtering [must be] for the sake of peace-offerings; and similarly regarding a sin-offering: "and he shall slaughter it for a sin-offering"; and similarly [regarding] the Pesach [offering]: "it is the sacrifice of the Passover." Nevertheless, certainly [in the case of] a Pesach [offering], whose primary purpose is to be eaten by its owners, if he slaughtered it not for the sake of its owners [in order] to feed it to other registered [participants], it is invalid, as the Mishnah teaches: "[If] he slaughtered it not for those registered for it, it is invalid." And perforce [the Mishnah] is speaking of where he intended [this] for the slaughtering alone, not on condition of throwing [the blood], since the Amoraim disagree about it in the Gemara [regarding the case where] "he slaughtered it for circumcised [people] on condition that uncircumcised [people] gain atonement through it" — from which it follows that "he slaughtered it for uncircumcised [people]" of our Mishnah is speaking of one who intends [this] regarding the slaughtering [itself], and "not for those registered for it" is similar to "for uncircumcised [people]," since it teaches them alongside one another.

Rashi on Pesachim 61a:1:3.hebrew: ואינו לאחר מיתה - דאין שם בעליו עליו מאחר שמת, ואם שינה שמו כשר:
Rashi on Pesachim 61a:1:3.english: And it does not [apply] after death - For its owner's name is not upon it once he has died, and if [the priest] changed his name, it is valid.

Rashi on Pesachim 61a:1:4.hebrew: ואינו בצבור - דלשם מי ישנה אותו שלא יהא בעליו? אם לשם נכרים, לא מיפסיל, כדאמרי' התם ולקמן בשמעתין דאין שנוי בעלים פוסל אא"כ שינהו למחויב כפרה כמותו, דיליף מלכפר עליו — עליו ולא על חבירו. אלמא שינוי בעלים פסול בחבירו דומיא דידיה ומחויב כפרה כמותו, ואי לא — לא פסיל:
Rashi on Pesachim 61a:1:4.english: And it does not [apply] to communal [offerings] - For in whose name could one change it so that [that person] is not its owner? If [one intends it] for the sake of gentiles, it is not disqualified, as we say there and later in our sugya, that a change of owner does not disqualify unless one changed it to [someone who is] obligated in atonement like himself, as it is derived from "to atone for him" — "for him," and not for his fellow. Thus, a change of owner disqualifies [only] with his fellow who is similar to him and obligated in atonement like himself, and if not, it does not disqualify.

Rashi on Pesachim 61a:2:1.hebrew: ואע"ג דתרתי - מהנך פירכי:
Rashi on Pesachim 61a:2:1.english: And even though two - [Two] of those refutations.

Rashi on Pesachim 61a:2:2.hebrew: לאו דווקא - כלומר, לאו פירכי נינהו; תרתי מיהא דווקא, ומפרש ואזיל הי תרתי לאו דווקא: פסול מחשבה לא מיקרי פסול הגוף:
Rashi on Pesachim 61a:2:2.english: Not exact - That is to say, they are not [valid] refutations; two [of them], however, are exact, and [the Gemara] proceeds to explain which two are not exact. A disqualification of thought is not called a disqualification of the body [of the offering].

Rashi on Pesachim 61a:3:1.hebrew: ולרב פנחס - בפ"ק דזבחים אמרה:
Rashi on Pesachim 61a:3:1.english: And according to Rav Pinehas - He stated it in the first chapter of Zevachim.

Rashi on Pesachim 61a:3:2.hebrew: יש בעלים לאחר מיתה - ואם שחטו לשם בעלים אחרים, צריך היורש להביא אחר:
Rashi on Pesachim 61a:3:2.english: There is an owner after death - And if one slaughtered it for the sake of another owner, the heir must bring another [offering].

Rashi on Pesachim 61a:4:1.hebrew: כמי שאין לו בעלים - כמי ששחטו בזמנו שלא לשם בעלים. ואני שמעתי: שינוי בעלים אינו בזריקה, כדאמרי' "אין מחשבת אוכלים בזריקה". ואי אפשר לומר כן, דמחשבת שלא לאוכליו — מנויין עליו הן, ובשחיטה הוא דגלי רחמנא, ולא בשאר עבודות; אבל מחשבת שלא למנויו, דהיינו שינוי בעלים, עיקרה בזריקה הוא, כדיליף לקמן בשמעתין בזריקה: "וכפר עליו" — ולא על חבירו:
Rashi on Pesachim 61a:4:1.english: Like one that does not have an owner - Like [a Paschal lamb] that one slaughtered in its [proper] time not for the sake of [its] owners. And I heard [that] a change of owners does not [apply] during sprinkling, as we say: "There is no [disqualifying] intention regarding eaters during sprinkling." But it is impossible to say so, for [in the case of] an intention not for its eaters, they are [nevertheless] registered upon it, and it is regarding slaughter that the Merciful One revealed [that it disqualifies], and not regarding the other services. However, [in the case of] an intention not for those registered upon it — which is a change of owners — its primary [application] is during sprinkling, as [the Gemara] derives later in our sugya regarding sprinkling: "And he shall make atonement for him" — and not for his fellow.

Rashi on Pesachim 61a:5:1.hebrew: לאוכליו ושלא לאוכליו כשר - דמקצת אוכלין לא פסלי, ולקמן מפרש טעמא:
Rashi on Pesachim 61a:5:1.english: For those who can eat it and for those who cannot eat it, it is valid - For a portion of eaters does not disqualify [the offering], and later [the Gemara] explains the reason.

Rashi on Pesachim 61a:6:1.english: Stirs its blood - So that it will not congeal, in order that it be fit for sprinkling.

Rashi on Pesachim 61a:6:2.hebrew: ואם נזרק - קודם לתמיד, כשר. דאע"ג דאמרן (לעיל פסחים ד' נט.) יאוחר דבר שנאמר בו בערב ובין הערבים וגו', לא מיפסיל בהכי:
Rashi on Pesachim 61a:6:2.english: And if it was sprinkled - before the daily offering, it is valid. For although we said (above, Pesachim 59a) [that] something regarding which "in the evening" and "between the evenings," etc. is stated should be postponed, it is not disqualified thereby.

Rashi on Pesachim 61a:8:1.hebrew: מכסת - לשון מנויין, כמו את מכסת הערכך (ויקרא כ״ז:כ״ג):
Rashi on Pesachim 61a:8:1.english: Number of [mikhsat] - [This is] an expression of registered [participants], like "the tally of your valuation" (Leviticus 27:23).

Tosafot on Pesachim 61a:10:1.hebrew: רבי אומר לשון סורסי הוא זה - אור"י, דרבי לא פליג את"ק, ומודה דאיכא עיכובא באוכליו ומנויו, ואינו אלא מפרש דבריו, דלא פסלי אוכליו ומנויו אלא בשחיטה. וכן משמע בכיצד צולין (ד עח:), דמסיק רב דאמר אכילה לא מעכבי כרבי נתן, ולא קאמר כר'; והיינו משום דלפרושי אתא כדפי':
Tosafot on Pesachim 61a:10:1.english: Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] says: This is Aramaic [Sursi] - Rabbi Yitzchak says that Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] does not disagree with the Tanna Kamma, and agrees that there is an indispensable requirement regarding its eaters and its registrants, and he is merely explaining his [the Tanna Kamma's] words: that its eaters and its registrants only disqualify [the offering] at [the time of] slaughter. And so it is implied in [the chapter] Keitzad Tzolin (78b), where [the Gemara] concludes that Rav, who says [that the requirement of] eating does not invalidate [the offering], follows Rabbi Natan, and it does not say [that he follows] Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi]; and that is because [Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi] came to explain [the Tanna Kamma's view], as I have explained.

Tosafot on Pesachim 61a:11:1.hebrew: לאוכליו מנא לן - אור"י דערלים וטמאים כולהו נפקי מהאי קרא ד"איש לפי אכלו", דכיון דלא מצו אכלי ליה, חשיבי כולהו שלא לאוכליו. וכן משמע בפ"ב דזבחים (ד' כב:), דקאמר: קסברי זקני דרום טמא משלח קרבנותיו; פי': פסח. והתניא: "במכסת נפשות" — מכאן שאין הפסח נשחט אלא למנויו, ואיתקש אוכליו למנויו. משמע בהדיא דטמא נפקא לן מ"איש לפי אכלו":
Tosafot on Pesachim 61a:11:1.english: [Not] for those who can eat it, from where do we [derive this] - Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that uncircumcised [men] and ritually impure [people] are all derived from this verse, "According to every man's eating" — for since they cannot eat it, they are all considered "not for those who can eat it." And so it is implied in the second chapter of Zevachim (22b), where [the Gemara] says: The Elders of the South hold that an impure person may send his offerings; explanation: [this refers to] the Paschal lamb. [And the Gemara objects:] But was it not taught in a baraita: "According to the number of the souls" — from here [we derive] that the Paschal lamb is slaughtered only for those registered for it, and those who eat it are juxtaposed to those registered for it? It is explicitly implied that [the disqualification of] an impure person is derived from "According to every man's eating."

Tosafot on Pesachim 61a:11:2.hebrew: ואיתקש אוכליו למנויו - תימה לר"י: א"כ, מה מנויו פסלי בד' עבודות, דהיינו שינוי בעלים, אף אוכליו יפסלו בד' עבודות, ובשאר קרבנות נמי יפסלו במנויו? וי"ל, דשלא למנויו אין זה שינוי בעלים; דשינוי בעלים לא פסיל אלא בזריקה, כגון שוחט או מקבל ומוליך על מנת לזרוק לשם אחרים, או זורק לשם אחרים, אבל שוחט ומקבל ומוליך לשם אחרים — כשר, דמוכפר עליו נפקא לן. ושלא למנויו היינו שוחט שלא למנויו, ולא פסיל אלא בשחיטה דווקא, כדכתיב "תכוסו", ודווקא בפסח ולא בשאר קרבנות. וא"ת: ונימא הואיל וגלי שלא לאוכליו בשחיטה, ה"ה בשאר עבודות, כדאי' בפ"ק דזבחים (ד' ז:) — פסח שלא לשמו מזבח פסח, שאר עבודות מנא לן? הואיל וגלי גלי! ואור"י, דלא דמי: כיון דגלי בכל הקרבנות דלא עלו לבעלים לשם חובה, וגבי פסח אשכחן פסול בחד מינייהו — אין לנו לחלק:
Tosafot on Pesachim 61a:11:2.english: "And those who eat it are juxtaposed to those who are registered for it" - This is puzzling to Ri: If so, just as [slaughtering for] those not registered for it disqualifies in [all] four [blood] services — which is [the case of] a change of owners — so too [offering for] those who cannot eat it should disqualify in [all] four services, and in other offerings as well [the offering] should be disqualified [if offered] for those not registered for it? And one can answer that [offering] for those not registered for it is not [the same as] a change of owners; for a change of owners disqualifies only in [connection with] the sprinkling [of the blood], such as one who slaughters, or receives and conveys [the blood], with the intent to sprinkle it on behalf of others, or one who sprinkles it on behalf of others, whereas one who slaughters, receives, or conveys [the blood simply] on behalf of others — it is valid, for we derive it from [the verse] "and atonement shall be made for him" [which refers to sprinkling]. And [offering] for those not registered for it means slaughtering for those not registered for it, and it disqualifies specifically in [the act of] slaughtering, as it is written "you shall make your count," and specifically with the Paschal lamb and not with other offerings. And if you ask: Let us say that since [Scripture] revealed [that] for those who cannot eat it [disqualifies] in slaughtering, the same applies to the other services, just as it is stated in the first chapter of Zevachim (7b) — [we derive that] a Paschal lamb [slaughtered] not for its own sake [is disqualified] from "and you shall sacrifice the Passover offering"; from where do we [know this for] the other services? Since it was revealed [for slaughtering], it was revealed [for all of them]! And Ri answers that it is not comparable: Since [Scripture] revealed regarding all offerings that [when offered not for their own sake] they do not count for the owners toward their obligation, and regarding the Paschal lamb we found disqualification in one of them [i.e., slaughtering] — we should not differentiate [between the services].

Tosafot on Pesachim 61a:1:1.hebrew: וישנו לאחר מיתה - ושינוי בעלים אינו לאחר מיתה, שמא משום דכתיב: "לכפר עליו" — ולא על חבירו, ומת לאו בר כפרה גמורה הוא, אלא שנתחייב להביאו. והך דשמעתין אתיא להדיא כמ"ד שיעבודא דאוריי', וכרב אסי אמר רב בפ"ק דקדושין (ד' יג:), דמוקי הא דתנן: "האשה שמתה — יביאו יורשין עולתה", אע"פ שלא הפרישתה מחיים. אבל לרב יהוד' אמר שמואל, דאמר: "והוא שהפרישתה מחיים, אבל לא הפרישתה — לא, משום דשיעבודא לאו דאורייתא", לכאורה אינו נפקותא בין שינוי קודש לשינוי בעלים דלאחר מיתה, כיון דבשינוי קודש [נמי] אין היורש חייב להפריש אחר תחתיו. ומיהו י"ל דנ"מ: אם הפרישו בעלים שתי עולות לאחריות, שאם תפסל האחת יביא השניה, ואם לאו תהא השניה חולין; אי נמי: שינוי קודש אסור לשנות אחר מיתה, דאמר בריש זבחים (ד' ב:): "ונדבה מי שרי לשנויי בה?", אבל שינוי בעלים ליכא אפי' איסור, כיון דאינו לאחר מיתה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 61a:1:1.english: "And it applies after death" - And a change of owner does not apply after death, perhaps because it is written, "to make atonement for him" — and not for his fellow, and a dead person is not subject to full atonement, rather [it is only] that he was obligated to bring it. And this [teaching] of our sugya accords explicitly with the one who says [that a] lien is by Torah law, and like Rav Asi said in the name of Rav in the first chapter of Kiddushin (13b), who establishes that which we learned in a Mishnah: "A woman who died — her heirs must bring her burnt-offering," even though she did not set it aside during her lifetime. However, according to Rav Yehudah [who] said in the name of Shmuel, who says: "And that is [only] if she set it aside during her lifetime, but if she did not set it aside, no, because a lien is not by Torah law," ostensibly there is no practical difference between a change of sanctity and a change of owner after death, since in [the case of] a change of sanctity as well the heir is not obligated to set aside another [offering] in its stead. Nevertheless, one can say that there is a practical difference if the owner set aside two burnt-offerings as a guarantee, so that if the one is disqualified he shall bring the second, and if not, the second shall be non-sacred; alternatively, [with] a change of sanctity it is forbidden to make a change after death, as it says at the beginning of Zevachim (2b): "And is it permitted to make a change in a freewill-offering?" — whereas [with] a change of owner there is not even a prohibition, since it does not apply after death.

Tosafot on Pesachim 61a:4:1.hebrew: נעשה כמי שאין לו בעלים בזמנו ופסול - תימה לר"י, ל"ל למימר "נעשה"? כיון דתרתי דוקא, לימא דפסול משום דאין כאן עקירה! ואי לא חייש להני פירכי, וסבר דדמי לשינוי קודש הואיל ופוסלו בזמנו וחשיב עקיר' — א"כ אמאי הוי כמי שאין לו בעלים בזמנו? הלא בשינוי קודש לא חשבי' משנה כבזמנו לפסול! ואור"י דהכי פי': אפי' ליתנהו להנהו פירכי, מ"מ לא הוי עקירה; דנעשה כפסח בזמנו שמתו בעליו, דאמר בסוף אלו דברים (פסחים ד' עג:) דבעי עקירה וכששחטו סתם פסול, אע"פ שהוא כמפרש שלא לשם בעליו, שהרי מתו; ה"נ שלא בזמנו שינוי בעלי' לא חשיב עקירה. וכן מוכיח הלשון, דקאמר "שאין לו בעלים", ולא קאמר "כמי ששחטו בשינוי בעלים":
Tosafot on Pesachim 61a:4:1.english: "It becomes like one that does not have an owner at its [proper] time, and it is disqualified" - This is astonishing to Ri: Why did [Rava] need to say "it becomes [like one that has no owner]"? Since the two [distinctions] are indeed accurate, let him [simply] say that it is disqualified because there is no uprooting [of the Paschal designation] here! And if he is not concerned about these refutations, and he holds that [a change of owner] is similar to a change of sanctity since it disqualifies it at its [proper] time and is considered an uprooting — if so, why is it like one that does not have an owner at its [proper] time? After all, in the case of a change of sanctity, we do not consider one who changes [it] as [if he were offering it] at its [proper] time so as to disqualify [it]! And Ri says that this is its explanation: Even if those refutations did not exist, nevertheless it is not [considered] an uprooting; for it becomes like a Paschal lamb at its [proper] time whose owner died, regarding which it is said at the end of [chapter] Eilu Devarim (Pesachim 73b) that it requires uprooting, and when one slaughters it without specification it is disqualified, even though it is as if he explicitly stated [that it is] not for the sake of its owner, since [the owner] died. Here too, not at its [proper] time, a change of owner is not considered an uprooting. And so too the wording proves [this], for it says "that does not have an owner," and it does not say "like one that he slaughtered with a change of owner."
